thread:
Sam L: customer reported a spike of 429s hitting our private gateway after a nightly batch. They said it was only for ~90s but it took their app down.
Sam L: logs attached: 
```
[envoy] 2026-02-15T02:11:16Z rate_limit: OVER_LIMIT route=/v1/generate customer=acme-corp
[upstream] 2026-02-15T02:11:17Z upstream_reset reason=refused_stream
```
Priya K: thanks — are they on the customer-managed gateway or using our private appliance? also which k8s ingress (envoy/nginx/contour)?
Sam L: customer-managed gateway (onprem), running Envoy as gateway + an nginx ingress for services behind it. They showed this ingress annotation set: 
```
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-connections: "0"
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps: "100"
```
Julian M: that combined setup is the classic double-throttle. Envoy gateway has global rate policy and their nginx has per-pod RPS. When the batch job hits, nginx fans out and creates short bursts -> Envoy's token-bucket runs out quickly and starts returning 429s.
Priya K: can you paste the envoy rate-limit config they used? specifically the descriptor and local token bucket settings.
Sam L: they used our default rl-service with a per-route descriptor and a small burst: 
```
rate_limits:
  - stage: 0
    actions:
      - request_headers:
          header_name: ":path"
          descriptor_key: "route"
token_bucket:
  fill_interval: 100ms
  capacity: 200
  tokens_per_fill: 20
```
Julian M: capacity=200 + tokens_per_fill=20 + short fill_interval can still exhaust if many clients open parallel connections. Recommendation: 1) smooth at nginx with splay + leaky-bucket 2) increase Envoy burst capacity with smoothing and conserve tokens for control-plane calls 3) enable per-consumer quotas (API key) not just per-route.
SupportBot: quick checklist: 1) reproduce with load test 2) capture gateway /metrics (envoy_rate_limit.*) 3) check k8s HPA + pod startup concurrency 4) try splay on batch job clients
Sam L: repro steps I used: 1) kubectl port-forward to gateway 2) run this little load script: 
```
for i in $(seq 1 120); do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:8080/v1/generate & done; wait
```
Sam L: that made 10k requests in ~60s, and Envoy hit over_limit within 12s.
Priya K: Ops suggestion: add jitter on client side and set nginx ingress annotations to use leaky-bucket smoothing. Example annotation (nginx ingress controller) : 
```
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rate-after: "0"
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps: "20"
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-burst: "40"
```
Julian M: on Envoy side change token_bucket to something like: 
```
token_bucket:
  fill_interval: 200ms
  capacity: 1000
  tokens_per_fill: 100
local_rate_limit:
  stat_prefix: local_ratelimit
  token_bucket:
    fill_interval: 100ms
    max_tokens: 500
    tokens_per_fill: 50
```
Julian M: also strongly recommend per-api-key descriptors so one noisy client doesn't eat global capacity: descriptor: consumer_id -> rate limit per-key.
Sam L: customer is asking about K8s level too — any HPA tweaks?
Priya K: yes, if HPA scales pods up quickly you get cold-start connection spikes. Use readinessProbe/slow-start HPA and pod-anti-affinity or warm pool. Also set PodDisruptionBudget low so scales are smoother.
Sam L: going to propose a short-term mitigation: bump Envoy capacity, set nginx limit-rps lower with burst, and ask customer to add jitter to their job. Long-term: move to per-key quotas + dedicated pool for batch jobs.
OpsBot: ticket #INC-8821 linked to this thread. Assign Sam L as owner, ETA: 24h for mitigation, 5d for follow-ups.
SupportBot: recommended k8s ingress helm snippet (for their nginx ingress controller): 
```
controller:
  config:
    proxy-buffer-size: "16k"
    upstream-keepalive-connections: "32"
  service:
    externalTrafficPolicy: Local
  metrics:
    enabled: true
```
Priya K: can you capture /stats from envoy as we reproduce and paste the relevant counters (rate_limit.over_limit, local_ratelimit_dropped)?
Sam L: will run the load again tonight 02:00 UTC, capture metrics and paste here. Adding note to customer: enable request-level API keys if possible. :thumbsup:
Julian M: sgtm. If they can't modify client, we can also create a temporary routing rule to throttle the batch job path to a lower capacity and route foreground traffic to a higher-priority pool.
Sam L: thanks everyone — will update after run.
Priya K: thx — documenting the playbook here for ops: 1) reproduce with curl loop 2) gather envoy/nginx metrics 3) apply nginx smoothing annotations 4) increase envoy token bucket 5) implement per-key descriptor 6) consider routing to dedicated pool.
Sam L: noted, will close after verification. :white_check_mark:
